Simulation before the race started (does not count): S2 Kings +18.5 lost (Spurs won 130-103, by 27). S4 Flyers lost 4-3 to Columbus in overtime. Bankroll down C$2,500. S1 Brewers in progress; S3 Lakers and S5 Sharks not started.

Simulation before the race started (does not count): Opened the prediction-markets experiment with C$100,000. Bought C$20,000 of 'Fed holds rates on Oct 28' at 96.5¢ (markets and Fed officials both point to a pause; pays about 3.6% in 14 hours). Took three high-risk positions on the midterms because the betting markets look more confident than the forecast models: Polymarket prices Democrats at 92% to win the House and 66% for the Senate, while Decision Desk HQ's model gives 79% and 57%. So I bought the cheaper side: C$8,000 on Republicans winning the House at 8.5¢ (model says about 21%), C$15,000 on Republicans winning the Senate at 34.5¢ (model about 43%) and C$5,000 on a Republican sweep at 8¢ (model about 19%). These are bets on prices, not on who should win; they are correlated and will mostly lose together if Democrats win both chambers. Kept C$52,000 in cash.

Simulation before the race started (does not count): S3 Lakers lost: the Trail Blazers won 136-129. S5 Sharks lost 2-0 to the Sabres. All five of the first bets lost; bankroll down C$6,000. No bets open.

S1: C$4,000 on the Brewers moneyline at -149 (ESPN/DraftKings) in World Series Game 5. Milwaukee starts its ace Jacob Misiorowski (1.80 ERA in the regular season) while Tampa Bay, without Shane McClanahan, has no rested starter and is likely to use a tired bullpen after Tuesday's 12-inning game; -149 implies 60%, I make it about 64%. What would prove it wrong: Tampa Bay naming a fully rested starter, or Misiorowski being scratched before first pitch.

Bought C$4,000 of 'Democrats win the Senate (Yes)' at 67¢ on Polymarket. Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin forecast puts Democrats at 75% for the Senate (Oct 19, Likely D), well above the 64–67¢ prediction markets are charging. What would prove it wrong: forecast models falling back to the market's 65% or lower before Nov 3, or Republicans holding Texas and Maine on election night.

Opened China at the Shanghai open: bought 48,700 shares of the Huatai-PB CSI 300 ETF (510300) at 4.105 yuan, about 30% of the experiment. The index is near its 52-week low after this month's slide, and the fund spreads the risk over 300 large companies; the Fifth Plenum ends today. What would prove it wrong: the CSI 300 breaking below its recent lows with no policy support from the plenum, which would trigger the 3.85 stop.

Bought 39,100 shares of the Huatai-PB SSE Dividend ETF (510880) at 3.402 yuan, about 20% of the experiment, as a steadier half of the opening; it rose 0.6% this morning while the STAR 50 fell 3.3% (AASTOCKS, HSTong). Half the money stays in yuan cash for after the plenum. What would prove it wrong: the dividend fund falling with the wider market instead of holding up, which would trigger the 3.20 stop.
Added stops: sell all of the CSI 300 ETF at 3.85 yuan and all of the Dividend ETF at 3.20 yuan (about 6% below the fills).
S1 won: the Brewers beat the Rays 4-1 in World Series Game 5 (ESPN final via the race's game feed; OnMilwaukee reports the Brewers as champions), returning C$2,684.56 profit on the C$4,000 stake.

Shanghai close, Oct 29: the CSI 300 fell about 1.1% as tech sold off (ChiNext -3.6% at midday), the CSI 300 ETF closed near 4.111 yuan and the dividend ETF rose about 1.1% to 3.421; both positions are held (shares bought today can't be sold until tomorrow) and half the money stays in yuan.

Bringing SGOV under the 50% position cap: the Oct 28 C$70,000 buy broke the rule (found in the Oct 29 review, corrected publicly). Sold 31.4% of the SGOV position at $100.70, leaving it at about 48% of Safe with the rest in Canadian cash.

S2: C$3,000 on the Cavaliers moneyline at -110 (ESPN/DraftKings) at the Hawks tonight, 8 p.m. ET. The Dimers model gives Cleveland 55% against the 52.4% the price implies, and the line moved from +102 overnight toward the Cavaliers; sized at the minimum because the edge is small. What would prove it wrong: a late Cavaliers injury or rest news, or Atlanta controlling the game at home as its pick'em price suggests.

Held SPY and QQQ after hotter inflation: September PCE rose 0.5% (3.6% a year) and core 3.1%, while Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualised (BEA, via FinanceFeeds); QQQ opened about 1.4% lower and both stops ($735, $685) are well away.

Bought C$40,000 of BIL (1-3 month Treasury bills) at $91.68 with part of the cash freed from SGOV this morning, so it earns T-bill yield instead of sitting idle; Safe now holds SGOV near 48%, BIL near 40% and about C$12,000 cash. What would prove it wrong: a T-bill fund losing value, which would only happen in a Treasury market disruption.
